{{Year in Japan|2000}}
The following lists events that happened during '''[[2000]] in [[Japan]]'''. It corresponds to the year [[Heisei]] [[12 (number)|12]] in the [[Japanese calendar]].

==Incumbents==
* [[Emperor of Japan|Emperor]]: [[Akihito]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Akihito {{!}} Biography, Reign, & Facts |url=https://www.britannica.com/biography/Akihito |website=Encyclopedia Britannica |access-date=27 March 2019 |language=en}}</ref>
* [[Prime Minister of Japan|Prime Minister]]: [[Keizo Obuchi]] ([[Liberal Democratic Party (Japan)|L]]–Gunma) until April 5, [[Yoshiro Mori]] (L–Ishikawa)
* [[Chief Cabinet Secretary]]: [[Mikio Aoki]] (Councillor, L–Shimane) until July 4, [[Hidenao Nakagawa]] (L–Hiroshima) until October 27, [[Yasuo Fukuda]] (L–Gunma)
* Chief Justice of the [[Supreme Court of Japan|Supreme Court]]: [[Shigeru Yamaguchi]]
* President of the [[House of Representatives of Japan|House of Representatives]]: [[Soichiro Ito (politician)|Sōichirō Itō]] (L–Miyagi) until June 2, [[Tamisuke Watanuki]] (L–Toyama) from July 4
* President of the [[House of Councillors]]: [[Jūrō Saitō]] (L–Mie) until October 19, [[Yutaka Inoue]] (L–Chiba)
* [[Diet of Japan|Diet]] sessions: 147th (regular, January 20 to June 2), 148th (special, July 4 to July 6), 149th (extraordinary, July 28 to August 9), 150th (extraordinary, September 21 to December 1)

==Events==

===January===
*January 26: The [[Southern All-Stars]] release "[[Tsunami (Southern All Stars song)|Tsunami]]", the best-selling CD single in Japanese history.

===February===
*February 6: [[Osaka Prefecture|Osaka]] gubernatorial election – Osaka's first female governor, [[Fusae Ohta]], is elected.

===March===
*March 4: [[Sony Computer Entertainment]]'s [[PlayStation 2]] goes on sale in Japan.
*March 8: [[Naka-Meguro train disaster]]
*March 31: [[Mount Usu]] in [[Hokkaido]] erupts for the first time in 23 years.

===April===
*April 1: [[Ritsumeikan Asia Pacific University]] opens in [[Ōita Prefecture]].
*April 2: Prime Minister [[Keizo Obuchi]] suffers a massive stroke and is hospitalized.<ref name="economist.com">{{cite news|url=https://www.economist.com/obituary/2000/05/18/keizo-obuchi|title=Keizo Obuchi|date=2000-05-18|newspaper=The Economist|access-date=21 April 2018}}</ref>
*April 4: Obuchi cabinet resigns.
*April 5: [[Yoshiro Mori]] is elected [[Prime Minister of Japan|Prime Minister]].

===May===
*May 14: Obuchi dies.<ref name="economist.com"/>
*May 15: [[Yoshiro Mori]] makes his first major gaffe, referring to Japan as a "divine nation centering on the Emperor."<ref>{{Cite news | url=http://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2000/05/27/national/mori-sorry-but-stands-by-quote/#.U-FGFfldXSE | title=Mori sorry but stands by quote| newspaper=The Japan Times Online| date=2000-05-27}}</ref>

===June===
*June to July: According to Japan Health and Welfare Ministry official confirmed report, an outbreak of [[food poisoning]] at [[Dairy|dairy factory]] in [[Osaka]], resulting to 13,420 people being infected, however, there were no reports of any deaths. This was confirmed by an Official, who said this incident was caused by [[enterotoxin]] in [[skimmed milk]].<ref>[:ja:雪印集団食中毒事件] '''(Japanese language edition)''' Retrieved date on 12 February, 2020.</ref>
*June 25: [[2000 Japanese general election|General election]] held.

===July===
*July 8: Volcanic eruption on [[Miyakejima]].
*July 19: [[Bank of Japan]] issues the first 2,000-yen banknotes.
*July 21–23: [[26th G8 summit|G8 Summit held in Nago, Okinawa]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mofa.go.jp/policy/economy/summit/2000/index.html|title=MOFA: Kyushu-Okinawa Summit|website=www.mofa.go.jp|access-date=21 April 2018}}</ref>

===August===
*August 1: New 500-yen coins enter circulation.

===September===
[[File:Nonami.jpg|thumb|right|150px|A torrential rain and flash flood in 2000 Nagoya flash flood]]
*September 2: Miyakejima is evacuated as the eruption continues.
*September 12: Heavy [[torrential rain]] and [[flash flood]] hits [[Nagoya]] and its suburbs, according to The Fire and Disaster Management Agency of Japan report, ten people lost their lives, with 115 people injured.<ref>[[:ja:東海豪雨]] '''(Japanese language)'''  Retrieved date on March 30, 2017</ref>
*September 19: The [[Mizuho Financial Group]] is established, becoming Japan's first [[bank holding company]].

===October===
*October 1: The DDI Corporation, the KDD Corporation and the ODI Corporation merge to become [[KDDI]].
*October 6: A magnitude 6.6 earthquake hits the city of [[Yonago, Tottori]], injuring 182 people.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Semmane|first1=Fethi|last2=Cotton|first2=Fabrice|last3=Campillo|first3=Michel|title=The 2000 Tottori earthquake: A shallow earthquake with no surface rupture and slip properties controlled by depth|journal=Journal of Geophysical Research|volume=110|issue=B3|pages=1, 2|doi=10.1029/2004jb003194|year=2005|url=https://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/hal-00109287/file/2004JB003194.pdf}}</ref>
*October 27: [[Chief Cabinet Secretary]] [[Hidenao Nakagawa]] resigns to take responsibility for a sex scandal he was embroiled in; [[Yasuo Fukuda]] is appointed in his place.
*November 5: After being exposed by ''[[Mainichi Shimbun]]'', archaeologist [[Shinichi Fujimura]] confesses to being a fraud; Japanese archaeologists had based their treatises on his findings.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-01-08 |title=Archaeologist faked finds at 42 sites {{!}} The Japan Times |url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2001/10/08/national/archaeologist-faked-finds-at-42-sites/#.XDQEr1PLfR8 |access-date=2023-07-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190108020214/https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2001/10/08/national/archaeologist-faked-finds-at-42-sites/#.XDQEr1PLfR8 |archive-date=2019-01-08 }}</ref>

===November===
*November 8: [[Japanese Red Army]] leader [[Fusako Shigenobu]] is arrested in Osaka.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/asia-pacific/1012780.stm|title=Japanese Red Army leader arrested|date=8 November 2000|access-date=21 April 2018|via=news.bbc.co.uk}}</ref>
